text:
lia: Heads up — noticed a small spike in resume failures + duplicate billing alerts right after we flipped the EU canary at ~09:03. Not a total outage but customers saw 1-3 extra token charges.

Tom: Any console traces? which change rolled to canary?

lia: It was the route prune change (prune-after reduced to 30s). I pasted a couple of short traces to #eng-platform-logs — proxy returned 204 on some midstream requests and clients retried to a fallback route.

alex: If prune kills the sticky lease then clients will reattach to fallback. Are fallback routes using the same quota namespace? I thought we aligned those.

maya: They shouldn't differ but I spot-checked a fallback mapping and the quota key is old-format: "quota:legacy:eu" vs new-format "quota:routes:eu-canary". That would explain billing mismatches.

lia: Timeline: canary flip 09:03:02, first 204s at 09:03:04, resume retries 09:03:06–09:03:40, duplicate billing alerts 09:03:20 onward.

Tom: Minimal repro locally: open SSE -> force prune -> proxy sends 204 -> client reconnects -> server emits two resume-ack events. Script below:

```
# repro
sse_pid=$(curl -s -N "https://api.redwood/v1/stream?client=test" & echo $!)
sleep 1
# trigger prune
curl -XPOST "https://console.internal/api/routes/prune?name=eu-canary"
sleep 1
kill -HUP $sse_pid
sleep 2
```

alex: Two immediate mitigations: 1) rollback prune-after to 5m for canary, 2) add a proxy-level idempotency token for fallback reattach (X-Fallback-Id). Rollback is fastest.

maya: Agreed on rollback for safety. Also we have low sampling on resume spans (0.5%) so traces are sparse. Can we crank resume sampling to 10% for the next 8h?

Tom: I'll flip sampling and bump prune-after for eu-canary to 300s. Preparing change.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Applying config change cfg-202404: sampling.resume=0.10, routes.eu-canary.prune_after=300s. Targets: 3 hosts. 1/3 updated.

lia: Also want a short-term alert: page if resume-failures > 5/min AND duplicate-billing > 1 in the same minute. Otherwise SRE won't see the correlation.

alex: Longer term: we should normalize fallback quota namespaces at route-config ingestion and show a console UI field: fallback_quota_namespace. Product/console UX will want a tooltip explaining semantics.

maya: +1. And implement X-Fallback-Id header in proxy so retries with same fallback id dedupe billing events server-side.

Tom: After the rollback + sampling bump we still saw 2 dup markers but rate dropped ~95%. Looks rollout timing was the trigger.

lia: Filing follow-up tickets: PROJ-1124 reconcile-fallback-quota-names, PROJ-1125 implement-x-fallback-id, PROJ-1126 console-fallback-namespace-ui.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: cfg-202404 applied to all hosts. Change complete.

alex: Great. Let's add a post-rollout checklist item: automatically increase resume sampling to 5-10% for 24h after any routing change. Visibility saves us here.

lia: Incident note saved: small billing duplication tied to route prune canary rollout. Mitigated by extending prune window + adding sampling + alert. Will follow up with postmortem if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
